title: Quarterly Sprint Orchestrator — Private Instance Capability Condenser & OKR Trace
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Create a repeatable quarterly sprint orchestration plan ("Sprint Orchestrator") that consolidates the set of Private/VPC/On‑prem capabilities we will deliver this quarter, maps each deliverable to explicit OKR signals, and defines clear failure buckets, acceptance gates, and runbooks for customer onboarding. The objective is to reduce activation time for new Private tenants by 40% and lower initial onboarding regressions (config, networking, auth) by 50% versus baseline.

Why this work matters:
- Customers adopting Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments cite unpredictable rollout windows and unclear preflight checks as top blockers.
- Multiple PM/ENG/Design tickets historically land in the same quarter but without a single coordination fabric; this causes scope creep and uncoordinated rollouts.
- Aligning deliverables to measurable OKR signals makes tradeoffs explicit and simplifies stakeholder communication.

Scope and deliverables (quarter):
1) Capability condenser: a prioritized, minimal set of features required for a "fast-path" private tenant activation lane (networking templates, KMS onboarding checklist, tenant config shim, telemetry enablement).
2) Sprint Orchestrator artifact: a cadence blueprint that sequences work across 6 two‑week sprints, with ownership, dependency map, and release windows.
3) Onboarding runbook + checklists: infra preflight, security review checklist, customer enablement steps, automated smoke test matrix.
4) OKR trace dashboard: per-feature signal wiring (activation time, provisioning success %, time‑to‑first‑payload, rollback occurrences) surfaced to Console and shared dashboard.
5) Failure buckets and rollback playbooks: defined failure categories (network, auth, capacity, data migrations), automatic mitigation paths, and customer communication templates.
6) Test harness and pilot: a reproducible test harness for tenant activation + a 3‑tenant pilot run with two lighthouse customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Activation time reduced (measurements captured in dashboard) and baseline established for Q-end reporting.
- Runbook and checklists published in Confluence and approved by Security & Ops.
- OKR trace dashboard deployed to shared Grafana + Console route; signals validated with synthetic activations.
- Pilot tenants successfully onboarded using the runbook; two pilot feedback items triaged and a plan created for remaining items.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Patel (lead), Miguel Torres (onboarding PM)
- Engineering: Infra (owner TBD), Runtime (ENG-1842), Ops/Platform SRE
- Design: Priya Shah (customer flows)
- Security & Compliance: Natasha Reed (KMS / audit log signoff)
- Customer Success: onboarding playbook and pilot coordination

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Networking templates may not cover customer's complex topologies. Mitigation: provide advanced config appendix and sandbox validation scripts.
- Risk: KMS integrations differ across clouds. Mitigation: certify two variants (AWS KMS, customer‑managed HSM) and provide fallback guidance.
- Risk: Dashboard signal noise. Mitigation: start with a small set of high‑signal metrics and iterate.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence draft (runbook): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/Private+Sprint+Orchestrator+Runbook
- Draft OKR wiring spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q_private_okr_wiring
- Pilot coordination sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/PrivateOnboardPilot2026
- Relevant PR/infra proof-of-concept: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-onramp/pull/412

Operational notes for execution:
- Weekly triage sync on Thursdays 09:00 PT with owners from Eng/Design/Security/CS.
- Sprint gating: every sprint end we run the smoke activation; if provisioning success < 90% the quarter escalates to contingency lane (remove next feature from scope and focus on stability).
- Rollout windows: define soft launch (pilot tenants) in week 8 and broader Tier‑1 enablement in week 12.

Longer term alignment:
This orchestrator will be a canonical template for subsequent quarters; feed learnings into the Private product playbook and convert checklist items into automation over the next two quarters.
